## python/carnot/verify/adaptive_conformal_calibration.py

**Verdict:** `HONEST_HEURISTIC`

## VERDICT
HONEST_HEURISTIC

## CLAIMS
“Compute a lightweight ACSE-style semantic entropy proxy.” The docstring explicitly says: “ACSE uses semantic dispersion over multiple generations,” but this corpus lacks fresh generations, so “this proxy uses two local uncertainty signals”: top-k logprob variance and cross-verifier score variance.

## IMPLEMENTATION_REALITY
The code performs deterministic lexical prompt classification, variance-based uncertainty scoring, group calibration, Fisher combination, and AUROC evaluation using NumPy and scikit-learn. It invokes no model; token logprobs and verifier scores are supplied as inputs.

DISCLOSED_PROXY

## GAMING_PATTERNS
none

## RECOMMENDATION
KEEP

## RATIONALE
The implementation is not ACSE semantic entropy: variance among token alternatives and unrelated verifier scores is a crude statistical surrogate. However, the docstring admits this limitation plainly, labels the calculation a “lightweight” proxy, and identifies exactly how it departs from the full method; there is no fake model claim or adversarial-check gaming.

## python/carnot/verify/beaver_lite.py

**Verdict:** `DISHONEST_NAMING`

## VERDICT
DISHONEST_NAMING

## CLAIMS
“BEAVER-lite probability-mass certificates for arithmetic answer constraints.”  
“llama.cpp logits-backed top-K prefix enumerator.”  
“Enumerate prefixes and bound unsafe probability mass for final answers.”

## IMPLEMENTATION_REALITY
The optional provider performs real llama.cpp inference and computes logits-backed beam candidates; otherwise it openly falls back to deterministic mock completions. However, it sums unsafe probability only within a pruned top-K frontier and labels that quantity an `upper_bound`, ignoring all omitted probability mass.

## CLAIM_VS_REALITY_GAP
UNDISCLOSED_PROXY

## GAMING_PATTERNS
none

## RECOMMENDATION
REIMPLEMENT_PROPERLY

## RATIONALE
The model substrate is real and the mock fallback is explicitly disclosed, so this is not regex masquerading as inference. The certificate claim is nevertheless false: unsafe mass observed in a truncated beam is not an upper bound on total unsafe mass unless unexplored mass is conservatively included. Its “soundness” check merely compares that mass against an empirical count rate—and is engineered to pass under the equal-mass mock—so this must not contribute to headline results as a certified bound.
